S 级 系统治疗 队列研究 IF 30.1
SIERRA研究：STRIDE方案用于不良预后不可切除肝癌的IIIb期单臂研究
First-line durvalumab and tremelimumab in poor-prognosis unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma: Phase IIIb single-arm SIERRA study
Journal of hepatology · 2026 Oct 6 · Chan SL, Kudo M, Sangro B 等
研究背景：STRIDE（单次替西木单抗+度伐利尤单抗）是不可切除肝癌（uHCC）一线标准方案之一，但III期HIMALAYA等关键试验排除了Child-Pugh B、ECOG 1-2及门静脉主干癌栓（Vp4）患者，而这类患者在临床中占比很高。
核心结果：SIERRA（NCT05883644）为IIIb期单臂研究，专门纳入上述不良预后人群。主要分析显示STRIDE在该人群中安全性可管理，疗效信号与总体人群方向一致，为不良预后人群使用STRIDE提供了前瞻性证据。
意义与启示：不良预后uHCC人群的一线免疫治疗证据长期空白，SIERRA以专门设计填补该空白；对临床实践而言，肝功能受损与癌栓患者的一线选择有了更直接的支持，也提示后续试验应减少对该人群的系统性排除。
评分明细：设计 24/30 · 验证 12/15 · 机制 6/15 · 影响力 15/20 · 契合度 20/20 = 77/100 ｜ 等级理由：IIIb期前瞻研究、直击真实世界最常见却长期被试验排除的人群，可能改变一线治疗选择与说明书人群界定

A 级 诊断与标志物 队列研究 IF 14.1
多中心大样本血清代谢标志物谱用于肝癌早诊（1924例发现队列）
Metabolic Signatures for Liver Cancer Diagnosis and Mechanistic Insights: A Large-Scale, Multicenter Study
Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) · 2026 Oct 4 · Xu Y, Wang J, Ding C 等
研究背景：肝癌预后差的核心原因是早诊率低，现有监测手段（AFP+超声）敏感性不足，亟需新的血液标志物组合。
核心结果：研究采用高通量纳米增强激光解吸/电离质谱对11个中心1924名参与者的血清代谢物建模，并在另2个中心225人独立外验；9-代谢物标志物联合AFP的判别AUC达0.92（发现）与0.93（外验）。
意义与启示：代谢组学标志物与AFP互补，有望纳入高危人群分层监测；若前瞻验证成立，将推动肝癌早诊从'影像+AFP'向多组学组合演进。
评分明细：设计 22/30 · 验证 13/15 · 机制 6/15 · 影响力 7/20 · 契合度 20/20 = 68/100 ｜ 等级理由：大规模多中心、独立外验、检测平台可及（纳米增强LDI-MS），早诊转化路径清晰

A 级 局部治疗 队列研究 IF 14.6
CHANCE2504：免疫+靶向±肝动脉灌注化疗治疗门静脉癌栓肝癌的全国目标试验仿真研究
Immunotherapy and targeted therapy plus hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy for HCC with portal vein tumor thrombosis (CHANCE2504): a nationwide target trial emulation study
Clinical and molecular hepatology · 2026 Oct 7 · Lin LW, Chen Q, Zhou JW 等
研究背景：合并门静脉癌栓（PVTT）的肝癌预后极差，治疗策略长期存在争议。免疫+靶向已成为一线标准，但在此基础上是否联合肝动脉灌注化疗（HAIC）缺乏高级别证据。
核心结果：CHANCE2504采用目标试验仿真（target trial emulation）与克隆删失加权（CCW）框架，整合全国36个中心的回顾性队列，比较HAIC+ICI+MTA三联与ICI+MTA双联的疗效与安全性。
意义与启示：在RCT难以覆盖的癌栓人群，目标试验仿真提供了接近随机的比较证据；若三联获益确立，将推动PVTT人群一线方案从'双联系统治疗'向'系统+局部'联合范式演进。
评分明细：设计 20/30 · 验证 11/15 · 机制 5/15 · 影响力 7/20 · 契合度 20/20 = 63/100 ｜ 等级理由：全国36中心目标试验仿真、方法学严谨，直接回答PVTT人群是否加用HAIC这一高争议临床问题

研究背景：高达40%的MASH相关肝癌发生于无肝硬化肝脏，其癌变机制与病毒性/酒精性肝癌不同，监测策略也难以覆盖。

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) depend on tumor biology and hepatic functional reserve. The albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade, developed by Johnson The aim of the study is to evaluate preoperative ALBI grade as a predictor of survival and postoperative complications after curative hepatectomy for HCC. This retrospective study included 333 patients undergoing curative-intent hepatectomy for HCC at a tertiary cancer center in India (2010-2023). ALBI grade was calculated from preoperative ALBI. Primary endpoint: overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints: posthepatectomy liver failure (PHLF), bile leak (PHBL), major complications (Clavien-Dindo ≥ IIIa), 6-month mortality, and recurrence-free survival (RFS). Multivariable logistic and Cox regression assessed ALBI as an independent predictor, with sensitivity analysis excluding the small, unstable ALBI grade 3 subgroup. ALBI grade distribution: grade 1 (54.4%), grade 2 (44.1%), grade 3 (1.5%). PHLF rose from 3.3% to 4.1% and 40% across grades ( Preoperative ALBI grade independently predicts survival, liver-specific complications, and early mortality after HCC hepatectomy, offering clinically accessible risk stratification complementary to tumor staging and supporting its integration into preoperative assessment and surgical decision-making. et al. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Macrovascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) confers extremely poor prognosis. While lenvatinib plus tislelizumab is an active targeted-immunotherapy regimen, local control of tumor thrombus remains suboptimal. Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) delivered via CyberKnife offers highly conformal local treatment and may have immunomodulatory effects. We evaluated whether adding CyberKnife SBRT to doublet systemic therapy was associated with improved outcomes in HCC with MVI. This real-world retrospective study included 116 HCC patients with MVI (Triple group: CyberKnife SBRT + lenvatinib + tislelizumab, The observed confirmed ORR was 68.0% (34/50) in the Triple Group versus 37.9% (25/66) in the Doublet Group; the stabilized IPTW-weighted ORR was 71.1% versus 37.6% ( In this selected cohort of patients with advanced HCC, MVI, preserved performance status, and Child-Pugh A/B7 liver function, the addition of CyberKnife SBRT to lenvatinib and tislelizumab was associated with higher confirmed response rates, longer local control, and prolonged PFS and OS, without a clear excess of severe toxicity. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), one of the most common malignancies worldwide, poses a major threat to the global health. Its prognosis depends heavily on early detection. Currently, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is the widely used biomarker for HCC diagnosis. Nevertheless, approximately 40% of the HCC cases do not produce AFP. It has been reported that the downregulation of miR-122 is strongly associated with the development and progression of HCC. Here, employing miR-122 as a biomarker, we developed a cascade amplification-based CRISPR-Dx platform for HCC diagnosis. Owing to the strong trans-cleavage activities of Cas13a and Cas12a, the proposed assay enabled sensitive miR-122 detection down to 1 aM. Clinical sample analysis (n = 48) demonstrated a sensitivity of 91.3%, a specificity of 84.0%, and an overall accuracy of 87.5%, which is significantly better than that of the conventional AFP-based diagnosis (sensitivity, 43.5%; specificity, 80%; accuracy, 62.5%). In addition, because CRISPR-Dx eliminates the RNA extraction and reverse transcription steps that may cause target loss, it also showed better performance than miR-122-targeted qPCR. Given its high diagnostic accuracy and simplified workflow, the proposed miR-122-based CRISPR-Dx assay holds great promise for the clinical diagnosis of HCC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Serum Raman spectroscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints for bioanalytical screening, but conventional models often rely on a single preprocessing pipeline. Because preprocessing can alter spectral distributions and attenuate information retained in raw spectra, this study developed a dual-channel fusion strategy for echinococcosis screening. We analyzed 573 serum samples from hepatic echinococcosis (HE), liver cirrhosis (LC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and normal controls (NC); 458 formed the development set and 115 were reserved for held-out testing. We developed a dual-channel convolutional neural network (DCNN) that fused complementary features from raw and preprocessed Raman spectra. Eight preprocessing pipelines and three fusion strategies were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold splits within the development set, and the configuration with the highest mean five-fold accuracy was fixed before held-out testing. The selected fusion strategy was then assessed across all eight pipelines against single-channel models. Under the locked configuration, the DCNN achieved 94.98% ± 1.62% mean accuracy, compared with 89.95% ± 4.36% for the preprocessed-spectrum CNN (P-CNN) and 88.42% ± 2.66% for the raw-spectrum CNN (R-CNN). Held-out accuracies were 95.65% for DCNN, 91.30% for P-CNN, and 89.57% for R-CNN. For binary screening, a DCNN trained on the development set achieved 96.52% accuracy on the held-out set, whereas the dot immunogold filtration assay (DIGFA) yielded 88.70% on the same samples. Feature-level fusion improved the use of complementary spectral information and reduced dependence on a single preprocessing pipeline. This strategy provides a robust framework for rapid, label-free serum Raman screening of echinococcosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The management of comorbidities has become increasingly relevant in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) as immunotherapy prolongs survival. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (AB) is a standard first-line option, but bevacizumab carries a risk of cardiovascular toxicities. Data on cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with cirrhosis remain limited. Identifying patients at increased cardiovascular risk is therefore clinically important, particularly given the availability of bevacizumab-free alternatives. We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the multicenter Italian ARTE database, including patients with uHCC treated with first-line AB between June 2022 and July 2025. Traditional major adverse cardiovascular events (tMACE) were defined as acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, cerebrovascular events, or peripheral ischemia, while an extended composite (eMACE) additionally included venous thromboembolism and immune-related myocarditis. Cardiovascular risk was stratified using the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Cardio-Oncology classification and the CARDIOSOR score. Competing-risk analyses were performed considering treatment discontinuation as a competing event. This study included 538 patients (median age 69.8 years). During follow-up, 20 patients (3.7%) experienced tMACE, and 30 (5.6%) experienced eMACE. Patients assigned to the very high-risk category by ESC criteria and those with a high-risk CARDIOSOR score had a significantly increased risk of tMACE and eMACE. Both scores demonstrated a moderate ability to stratify cardiovascular risk (Harrell's c-index 0.68 for ESC and 0.59 for CARDIOSOR). Cardiovascular adverse events were uncommon overall, but their incidence was not negligible in patients in high-risk subgroups. Risk scores may help identify vulnerable subgroups and support patient-tailored treatment strategies, including consideration of bevacizumab-free regimens in selected cases. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) cure most chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections, but their impact on liver functional reserve in patients with a history of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly after non-curative HCC treatment, remains unclear. We evaluated antiviral efficacy and liver functional reserve after DAA therapy according to HCC history and timing of DAA initiation. In this retrospective single-center cohort, 716 patients initiated DAA therapy, and 690 with evaluable sustained virological response at 12 weeks after treatment (SVR12) were analysed. Patients were classified as no HCC, curative-treated HCC, or non-curative-treated HCC according to the most recent HCC treatment before DAA initiation. Liver functional reserve was assessed using the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score, modified ALBI grade, and Child-Pugh class. In the non-curative-treated HCC group, early (≤ 3 months) versus delayed (> 3 months) DAA initiation after the most recent HCC treatment was compared. Overall SVR12 was 96.1%, with similarly high rates across groups regardless of HCC history. The median ALBI score improved from -2.35 to -2.58 at SVR12 in the curative-treated HCC group (p < 0.001) but remained unchanged in the non-curative-treated HCC group (-2.36 to -2.38). Among 64 patients with a history of HCC, 43 (67.2%) developed recurrence; in these patients, the ALBI score improved from -2.31 at DAA initiation to -2.57 at recurrence (p < 0.001), and more than 90% remained Child-Pugh class A. Early and delayed DAA initiation showed similarly high SVR12 rates and comparable liver functional reserve. DAAs achieved high SVR12 rates and maintained liver functional reserve in patients with HCV, including those with a history of HCC after non-curative treatment.

Physical activity (PA) confers several health benefits; however, whether increasing PA among physically inactive adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is associated with lower risks of adverse clinical outcomes remains unclear. We used the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database. We included 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at the initial health screening (Exam 1) and completed a subsequent screening within 4 years (Exam 2). Among them, 58,703 initiated moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), defined as vigorous activity ≥ 20 min/day on ≥ 3 days/week or moderate activity ≥ 30 min/day on ≥ 5 days/week. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcomes were liver-related events (hepatic decompensation, liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma [HCC]) and HCC. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Grey competing-risk models were adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioural factors. During a median 7.9-year follow-up (IQR, 5.2-9.5), 7609 deaths occurred. MVPA initiation was associated with lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), a lower risk of liver-related events (subdistribution HR [subHR], 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and, more modestly, of HCC (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared with those remaining inactive. The association was more pronounced in older adults, women, never smokers, non-drinkers, and untreated participants (all p for interaction ≤ 0.03). Initiating MVPA among physically inactive adults with CHB was associated with lower risks of mortality and liver-related outcomes. These findings provide large-scale epidemiological evidence supporting further evaluation of PA promotion in physically inactive patients with CHB.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Glypican-3 (GPC-3) is a cell-surface glycoprotein, highly expressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) but largely absent in normal adult liver tissues, making it a clinically compelling biomarker and therapeutic target. Although monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates have proven to be GPC-3-targeted therapies, their large molecular size, slow pharmacokinetics, and potential immunogenicity limit their diagnostic applications. Peptide ligands offer an attractive alternative owing to their low molecular weight, rapid tumor penetration, favorable clearance profiles, synthetic accessibility, and ease of chemical modification. This topical review highlights the development of linear and cyclic GPC-3-binding peptides over the past two decades, developed primarily via phage display, rational optimization, and structure-guided approaches, enabling PET, SPECT, and fluorescence imaging of HCC in preclinical models. Recent refinements, including albumin-binding modifications and cyclization strategies, have improved tumor-to-liver contrast and in vivo stability. This review summarizes the biological significance of GPC-3, compares peptides and peptide probes as targeting modalities, and critically analyzes recent advances in linear and cyclic peptide-based GPC-3 imaging probes. We also emphasized the importance, current challenges, and future opportunities in AI/ML-based design of peptide ligands for HCC theranostics.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer-associated mortality worldwide. Heterogeneity presents a notable challenge to the diagnosis and treatment of HCC and contributes to poor clinical outcomes. Exosomes serve key roles in intercellular communication among tumor cells and between malignant cells and components of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Accumulating evidence has indicated that exosomal cargo influences hepatocarcinogenesis, tumor progression, metastasis and remodeling of the TME. Accordingly, exosomal components present potential as biomarkers for early HCC detection and as therapeutic targets or delivery vehicles. The present review summarizes exosome biogenesis, isolation, characterization and functional heterogeneity, with particular emphasis on vesicle subpopulations, cellular origin, cargo composition, recipient-cell tropism, disease stage and microenvironmental stress. In addition, the evidence supporting exosome-based biomarkers and therapeutic applications in HCC are critically evaluated. Despite a number of candidates having shown promising results in preclinical or retrospective studies, to the best of our knowledge, no exosome-derived biomarker has yet been incorporated into routine clinical practice for HCC, highlighting the need for methodological standardization and prospective multicenter validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are widely incorporated into first-line treatment regimens for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Nevertheless, the growing incidence of immune-related adverse events (irAEs), particularly dermatologic toxicities, poses a substantial challenge to the continuation of anticancer therapy. The present study describes a case of tislelizumab-associated psoriasis in a patient with hepatitis C virus (HCV)-related HCC, emphasizing the need for prompt recognition and individualized management. A 60-year-old man with stage IIIA HCC and chronic HCV infection developed progressively worsening erythematous plaques with scaling during the eighth cycle of tislelizumab plus bevacizumab. Histopathological examination of a skin biopsy supported a diagnosis of pustular psoriasis. A Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale score of 7 suggested that tislelizumab was the probable causative agent. Because the patient had type 2 diabetes mellitus and declined systemic glucocorticoid treatment, tislelizumab was discontinued, and narrow-band ultraviolet B (NB-UVB) phototherapy was administered in combination with topical corticosteroids. The skin lesions markedly resolved with no recurrence during the 6-week follow-up period. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of NB-UVB phototherapy successfully treating ICI-induced psoriasis. This case underscores the need for close monitoring of cutaneous irAEs during ICI therapy and suggests that NB-UVB phototherapy may be an effective alternative to systemic corticosteroids for managing ICI-induced psoriasis, particularly in patients where preservation of antitumor immunity is desirable or systemic steroids are contraindicated. Regular multidisciplinary follow-up and individualized management of adverse events are essential for optimizing both oncological and dermatological outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (r-HCC) remains a major determinant of post-transplant (LT) outcomes. The 2024 ILTS-ILCA consensus highlighted the need for contemporary data assessing how evolving selection criteria and therapeutic strategies over the past 15 years have influenced prognosis. We conducted a retrospective study including all patients diagnosed with r-HCC following LT between 2008 and 2020 across 15 French transplant centres. Recurrence patterns, post-recurrence survival, and overall transplant outcomes were analysed, including temporal trends and the impact of AFP model implementation in 2013. We analysed 388 patients with r-HCC, median time to recurrence was 19.1 months, with 26.3% occurring beyond 3 years. Earlier recurrence was associated with tumour-related factors (AFP and Milan criteria, αFP kinetics), and later recurrence with patient-related factors (HCV recurrence, alcohol relapse, grade 2 obesity). Following AFP model implementation, time to recurrence shortened (p<0.001). Surgical/ablative treatments improved survival in r-HCC in a subgroup of patients with single organ involvement of liver, lung or lymph nodes. Survival did not improve between patients diagnosed before 2016, between 2016 and 2018, or after 2018 (p=0.09). Calcineurin inhibitors or mycophenolate mofetil had no impact on survival, whereas mTOR inhibitor use was associated with significantly longer survival (20.7 vs 13.2 months, p=0.001). r-HCC is a heterogeneous disease distinct from HCC in non-transplanted patients. Earlier recurrences following extended selection criteria implementation warrant caution. Surgical/ablative approaches should be prioritized even for extrahepatic disease. Despite expanded TKI options since 2016, outcomes of systemic treatment did not show statistical improvement. Post-recurrence mTOR inhibitors should be evaluated in clinical trials. This nationwide cohort study provides updated data on recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after liver transplantation in the modern era, a special population excluded from major HCC trials, highlighting major heterogeneity in patients' trajectories before and after recurrence, variations across eras of selection criteria and systemic therapies, and an urgent unmet need as the approval of second-generation TKIs after 2016 did not incrementally improve survival. The study results are important for transplant hepatologists and liver oncologists to optimize patient selection for liver transplantation, to individualize prolongation of surveillance beyond the current ILTS-ILCA 3-year window recommendation based on patient-related risk factors for late recurrences, and prioritize radical treatments with curative intent for selected patients with single organ involvement of liver, lungs or lymph nodes, rather than a blanket systemic-only approach. The retrospective design of the analysis does not allow for formal demonstration of superiority of therapeutic strategies, but provide evidence to design clinical trials on newer systemic agents such as immune-checkpoint inhibitors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The impact of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development after hepatitis C virus (HCV) elimination remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to clarify this association in a cohort of patients stratified by fibrosis severity. We analyzed the data of 2,596 eligible patients obtained from a multicenter database between 2014 and 2025. The FIB-4 index was used to assess fibrosis status, with patients categorized into three groups: <1.45, 1.45-3.25, and >3.25. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models were used to evaluate factors independently associated with HCC development. The median follow-up duration was 6.7 years. MASLD was present in 975 patients (36.3%) and was more frequent among men and patients with diabetes. During follow-up, 156 patients (6.0%) developed de novo HCC. Patients with MASLD had a higher cumulative incidence of HCC than those without MASLD (log-rank test, P<0.001); however, no HCC occurred in patients with FIB-4<1.45. MASLD was associated with HCC development in multivariable analysis of the overall cohort and in patients with FIB-4 1.45-3.25 and >3.25. Older age, male sex, lower albumin level, and higher AFP level at post-treatment week 12 were also independently associated with HCC development, whereas individual cardiometabolic risk factors were not significant after adjustment. MASLD was significantly associated with an increased risk of HCC after HCV cure, even among patients with intermediate FIB-4 values of 1.45-3.25. These findings support the need for tailored surveillance and management strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Repeat hepatectomies are challenging due to adhesions and altered anatomy. Robotic surgery, with enhanced dexterity and visualization, may expand the role of minimally invasive liver surgery (MILS) in this setting. The aim of this study was to explore the safety and efficacy of robotic repeat hepatectomy. We conducted a retrospective cohort study comparing repeat robotic (R-RLR), laparoscopic (L-RLR), and open liver resections (O-RLR) performed between January 2019 and December 2024. The primary outcome was postoperative morbidity. Secondary outcomes included conversion to laparotomy, use of Pringle maneuver, blood loss, hospital stay and postoperative mortality. For oncologic efficacy, rates of negative surgical margins (R0) or equivalent (R1 vascular), recurrences and survival were assessed. Forty-two patients underwent repeat hepatectomy (O-RLR = 15, L-RLR = 13, R-RLR = 14). Over time, O-RLR and L-RLR declined in favor of R-RLR. Main indications were colorectal liver metastases and hepatocellular carcinoma. Groups had similar age and comorbidities; however, cirrhosis and portal hypertension were more frequent in R-RLR. Mean Iwate scores were 6 (O-RLR), 4 (L-RLR), and 5 (R-RLR) (p = 0.240). Postoperative morbidity was significantly lower in L-RLR (7.6%) and R-RLR (7.7%) compared to O-RLR (40%) (p = 0.030). Mean Comprehensive Complication Index was 11.7 (O-RLR), 0.7 (L-RLR), and 0.6 (R-RLR) (p = 0.025). Two L-RLR cases required conversion. Pringle maneuver, blood loss, and hospital stay decreased progressively from O-RLR to L-RLR to R-RLR. There was no postoperative mortality.R0 resection was achieved in 73% (O-RLR), 100% (L-RLR), and 78.5% (R-RLR); R1 vascular rates were 13.3%, 0%, and 21.5%, respectively (p = 0.14). The three groups had similar overall and hepatic recurrence rates; survival (recurrence-free and overall) was also similar. Repeat robotic hepatectomy is safe and provides good oncologic outcomes. The robotic approach may allow MILS in more complex cases, including patients with cirrhosis and portal hypertension.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sorafenib is currently among the recommended first-line medications for patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, response to sorafenib remains unpredictable despite efforts to define prognosis. This study aims to predict treatment response and survival in patients with sorafenib-treated HCC using neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade, CRAFITY score, and Glasgow prognostic score (GPS). This prospective study recruited 75 Egyptian patients with Sorafenib-treated HCC. Pretreatment laboratory parameters and imaging studies were obtained. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, ALBI grade, CRAFITY score, and GPS were calculated for each patient. All the patients were followed for treatment response, overall survival, and sorafenib tolerance. Most of the participants were males, with a median age of 62 years. HCV was the most common underlying cause. Most of the patients had a low pretreatment NLR (77.33%), grade 2 ALBI (65.33%), 41.89% had a high CRAFITY score, and 48.6% had GPS 1. Patients were divided into two groups: group 1: sorafenib-naïve (n = 44) and group 2: patients with previous interventional therapy (n = 31). Pretreatment AST, ALT, mild ascites, portal invasion, and BCLC stage C were significantly higher among sorafenib-naïve patients. Median OS and time to progression for the entire cohort were 4 months and 9 months, respectively. No significant differences were observed in terms of OS between various NLR, ALBI grades, CRAFITY scores, and GPS. Multivariate analysis showed a high risk of mortality among sorafenib-intolerant patients (p = 0.01, HR: 2.33, 95% CI: 1.23-4.42). Overall survival and time to progression are not affected by different pretreatment values of NLR, ALBI grade, CRAFITY score, and Glasgow prognostic score in sorafenib-treated HCC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Development of therapies that selectively inhibit cancer cells but leave normal cells untouched is an important impediment to progress in cancer therapy. This paper reports the novel strategy employing the R-Tf-D-LP4 peptide, an unconventional cell penetrating peptide selectively targeting liver cancer cells, combined with the potent antitumor cytokine interleukin 15 (IL-15), with selective activity towards liver cancer cells. The fusion protein was constructed as a chimera between the IL-15 and the targeting peptide R-Tf-D-LP4 to improve the targeting specificity of this protein to the desired cells. With the help of modern computer modeling technologies, a fusion protein was designed, and its interactions with the IL-15 receptor complex (IL-15Rα/IL-15Rβ/γc) were evaluated using a molecular docking technique. The structure and physicochemical properties of the chimeric protein were determined using programs such as trROSETTA, I-TASSER, and ProtParam, after which they were further verified using SAVES 6.1 server with an excellent ERRAT quality score of 99.35%. Molecular docking using ClusPro 2.0, along with interaction evaluation using PDBsum program, demonstrated stability of the complex and strong hydrogen bonds and salt bridge interactions. The results were verified using the Desmond module in Schrödinger software to simulate molecular dynamics, which revealed a stable structure and proper functioning of the complex in physiological conditions. The expression analysis forecasted good yields from E. coli fermentation. The construct of the IL15/R-Tf-D-LP4 protein gene was created and inserted into the pET-22b ( +) vector, which was then transformed in BL21 (DE3) cells. The recombinant fusion protein was obtained by affinity chromatography and tested for purity by SDS-PAGE and western blotting. Cytotoxicity activity of the fusion protein was evaluated against the HepG2 cell line with the MTT test. As a result, the cytotoxic effect with an IC50 value of 23 μg/ml was established, compared to the non-chimera protein's IC50 value of 62 μg/ml. The achieved results allow us to speak about the prospects of using IL-15/R-Tf-D-LP4 fusion protein for clinical purposes in the future.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The therapeutic efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is frequently compromised by inherent apoptotic evasion and a hostile tumor microenvironment (TME). Inducing immunogenic cell death, particularly pyroptosis, represents a promising avenue to breach these barriers. Herein, we identify acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family member 11 (ACAD11) as a pivotal metabolic regulator that drives the ROS/NLRP3/GSDMD pyroptotic signaling axis. To therapeutically exploit this mechanism, we engineered a biomimetic delivery nanoplatform comprising cRGDyk-decorated platelets loaded with ACAD11-overexpressing plasmids (OE-ACAD11@R-PLT). By synergizing the intrinsic tumor-homing capabilities of platelets with cRGDyk-mediated active targeting, this system ensures precise accumulation in HCC tissues and facilitates efficient intracellular payload internalization. Upon cytosolic delivery, restored ACAD11 triggers severe mitochondrial dysfunction and subsequent GSDMD-executed pyroptosis. This lytic cell death releases a surge of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs), effectively remodeling the immunosuppressive TME into a highly immunogenic and pro-inflammatory milieu, thereby provoking a systemic anti-tumor immunity. Collectively, this work establishes a mechanism-driven, bioengineered strategy that leverages metabolic reprogramming to overcome therapeutic resistance, offering a robust paradigm for next-generation HCC nanomedicine.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Breast cancer liver metastasis (BCLM) represents a major clinical challenge. Characterizing the differences between primary and metastatic tumors could help identify therapeutic targets for preventing and treating metastasis. Through single-cell transcriptomic sequencing of matched primary tumors and BCLMs from 13 treatment-naïve patients, we uncovered a fundamental paradox in metastatic progression: BCLMs exhibited a highly immune-infiltrated microenvironment characterized by cytotoxic T cell expansion, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and depletion of regulatory T cells, yet they successfully evaded immune-mediated destruction. Metastatic cells retained extensive clonal and genomic diversity from their primary tumors, suggesting a polyclonal metastatic process rather than a stringent metastatic "bottleneck". Instead, cancer cells featured a metabolic adaptation mechanism in which elevated glutathione (GSH) metabolism in the liver fosters glutamine addiction, creating liver metastasis susceptibility. Integrative regulatory network analyses pinpointed NRF2 as a key regulator associated with GSH metabolism, and functional experiments demonstrated that GSH promoted tumor stemness and attenuated CD8⁺ T cell-mediated antitumor immunity in an NRF2-dependent manner. Inhibition of NRF2 and GSH reduced liver metastasis in vivo and was associated with enhanced antitumor immune responses. Together, this study provides comprehensive single-cell characterization of the immune-metabolic landscape in treatment-naïve BCLM and reveals a potential model in which metastatic success in immune-competent tissues depends on tumor cell-intrinsic metabolic adaptation. These findings provide insights into breast cancer liver metastatic progression and suggest NRF2 and GSH inhibition as a promising therapeutic strategy that could restore immune surveillance in liver metastases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lenvatinib is the most widely used first-line treatment for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Nevertheless, drug resistance remains a major clinical challenge, highlighting the need to identify the underlying mechanistic drivers. Here, we identified a role for annexin A1 (ANXA1) in promoting lenvatinib resistance by supporting endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria communication. Live-cell structured illumination microscopy revealed that ANXA1 deficiency induced the dissociation of ER-mitochondria contact sites (ERMCS), and Ca2+ kinetic analysis revealed that ANXA1 enhanced mitochondrial Ca2+ coupling. ANXA1 promoted ERMCS by directly binding the ER-mitochondria Ca2+ transfer tethers GRP75 and ITPR1 and promoting their interaction. Functionally, ANXA1 sustained oxidative phosphorylation following lenvatinib treatment and promoted cell survival. We further found that ANXA1 RNA stability was governed by an 8-oxoguanine modification-mediated ROS feedback loop. Therapeutically, photoacoustic imaging-guided in vivo analyses demonstrated that targeting this epigenetic-organelle communication feedback loop resensitized HCC to lenvatinib treatment, inhibiting peritumoral angiogenesis and improving the intratumoral hypoxic microenvironment. These findings uncover ERMCS formation as a driver of lenvatinib resistance in HCC, establishing a potential therapeutic strategy for targeting organelle communication to reverse drug resistance.

Despite widespread use of combination immunotherapy in advanced liver cancer, reliable biomarkers for baseline risk stratification remain lacking. The inflammatory cytokine interleukin-6 has established prognostic relevance in this cancer. We investigated the prognostic value of interleukin-6 and developed a combined score (ALBI-6) integrating interleukin-6 with albumin-bilirubin grade, a marker of liver function. In this multicentre retrospective cohort study, 216 patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab were analysed. Interleukin-6 was measured at baseline, first response, best response, and progression. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set (n = 98) and a validation set (n = 90). ALBI-6 was derived using Cox regression and evaluated against several established prognostic scores. Elevated baseline interleukin-6 was consistently associated with worse overall survival and remained independently prognostic after adjustment for tumour and clinical factors (extrahepatic spread, vascular invasion, alpha-fetoprotein, performance status, liver function class). In the validation cohort, ALBI-6 achieved a concordance index of 0.716 and separated patients into three risk groups with significantly different survival (log-rank p = 0.002); ALBI-6 was significantly more discriminative than one comparator score (modified albumin-bilirubin grade, p = 0.040), with numerically higher performance than the remaining comparators. In a separate analysis of the full cohort, ALBI-6 significantly outperformed the CRAFITY score at all assessed time points. Bootstrap validation confirmed model stability. ALBI-6 integrates systemic inflammation and liver function into a simple composite index enabling meaningful risk stratification in patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma treated with immunotherapy. Prospective external validation is warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Data on the geoepidemiology and phenotype of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) among individuals in Asia are limited. AIH patients were identified from the Taiwan National Health Insurance administrative database (n=24,867,461) with the ICD-10 CM code K75.4. A total of 8909 AIH patients (females, n=6018) were included. The average age- and sex-adjusted prevalence (2016-2023) and incidence rates (2017-2023) were 20.505 per 100,000 population and 4.739 per 100,000 population per year, respectively. The overall annual percentage changes for prevalence and incidence were 25.56% (p<0.0001) and 4.85% (p<0.0001), respectively. Compared with AIH patients in southern Taiwan, AIH patients in northern Taiwan accounted for the majority (72.70%) and were younger at diagnosis (54.17 vs. 55.62 years, p=0.0011). The 8-year liver cirrhosis (LC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), liver transplantation (LT), mortality and LT-free mortality cumulative incidence rates (CIRs) were 19.21%, 3.78%, 1.48%, 21.12% and 20.93%, respectively. The 8-year CIRs for hypertension, hyperlipidemia and diabetes were 44.77%, 46.84%, and 32.24%, respectively, and these diseases were the most common extrahepatic diseases. Lower hepatic and cardiometabolic complications and mortality but higher autoimmune complication CIRs were detected in northern than in southern Taiwan AIH patients. Higher hepatic and autoimmune complications but lower cardiometabolic complications and mortality CIRs were detected in female than in male AIH patients. Sex, age, residency, income, hepatic complications, diabetes and hyperlipidemia were associated with LC; sex, age, LC, ascites and diabetes were associated with HCC; and sex, age, residency, income, diabetes, hepatic complications, hyperlipidemia, systemic lupus erythematosus, thyroid diseases, systemic sclerosis and non-HCC cancers were associated with LT-free mortality. In Taiwan, the prevalence and incidence rates of AIH have increased over time. Care tailored to the patient's sex, age, residency, income and different complications is needed to improve outcomes.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To explore the effectiveness of rapid-resorbable gelatin microspheres (RGMs) for protecting non-tumorous liver (NTL) through flow modulation during yttrium-90 (Y-90) radioembolization for liver cancer. This phase II trial defined the primary outcome as the protection rate of RGM-embolized vs non-embolized NTL on Y-90 PET/CT. RGMs (560-800 µm) were used to transiently diminish blood flow to the NTL, followed by Y-90 microsphere administration. The effectiveness of flow modulation and radioembolization was assessed using Y-90 PET/CT and gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI (EOB-MRI). Twenty patients were enrolled between March 2023 and January 2025. The median protection rate was 35.8% (interquartile range [IQR], 20.2-66.7). Seven patients (35%, 7/20) demonstrated a ≥ 2-fold increase in the tumor-to-NTL uptake ratio on Y-90 PET/CT compared with pre-treatment SPECT/CT. The signal intensity (SI) ratio between protected and unprotected NTLs on the hepatobiliary phase of EOB-MRI increased significantly from baseline (median, 1.03; IQR, 0.97-1.05) to 6-month follow-up (median, 1.29; IQR, 1.18-1.54; p < 0.001). The Y-90 microsphere load to the NTL was negatively correlated with the protection rate (ρ = -0.578, p = 0.010), whereas the protection rate was positively correlated with the SI ratio at 6 months (ρ = 0.710, p = 0.001). All patients who underwent subsequent intra-arterial treatments achieved complete arterial recanalization. RGM-mediated flow modulation was associated with reduced Y-90 microsphere deposition in the NTL, with imaging findings suggesting regional liver function preservation. This protective effect appeared greater with lower Y-90 microsphere load. Question Can flow modulation using RGMS preserve regional liver function? Findings Prior embolization with rapidly resorbable gelatin microspheres reduced the absorbed dose to the NTL by 35.8% and preserved signal intensity on EOB-MRI after radioembolization. Clinical relevance RGMs can transiently divert arterial flow away from the NTL, reducing Yttrium-90 microsphere influx and helping preserve regional liver function during Yttrium-90 radioembolization for liver cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A residual risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) persists despite the use of nucleos(t)ide analogs (NA) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. We aimed to assess the utility of baseline serum laminin gamma 2 monomer (LG2m) by integrating PAGE-B score to predict HCC. NA-treated CHB patients whose baseline serum LG2m, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and PAGE-B score were measured. We evaluated the predictive value of LG2m in subgroups stratified by cirrhosis status and PAGE-B score and proposed a HCC surveillance algorithm. HCC developed in 56 of 1016 patients over a follow-up of 3651 person-years (annual incidence: 1.53%). None of the low PAGE-B patients developed HCC over 5 years. LG2m did not significantly stratify risk in high PAGE-B patients. Conversely, LG2m was significantly predictive of HCC in nonhigh PAGE-B patients (5-year incidence: 5.5% vs. 1.0% for high vs. low LG2m, p = 0.004). Integrating LG2m, AFP, and high PAGE-B achieved a sensitivity of 98.2% for HCC detection. Among patients with a nonhigh PAGE-B score, elevated LG2m was associated with a higher risk of HCC (adjusted HR, 4.40; 95% CI, 1.26-15.44), whereas AFP did not significantly stratify HCC risk in a separate analysis. Intermediate PAGE-B patients with high LG2m should receive closer HCC surveillance (annual incidence: 1.4%) as with high PAGE-B patients did (annual incidence: 1.9%). Serum LG2m level was predictive of HCC specifically among patients with intermediate PAGE-B score. Integration of LG2m into a PAGE-B-oriented algorithm provides a biomarker-driven tool for individualized surveillance, which is vital for improving early-stage HCC detection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This report details a 55-year-old male with liver metastases from Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma (ACC), enrolled in a study on Boron Neutron Capture Therapy (BNCT) utilizing Boronophenylalanine (BPA) as a carrier. The patient underwent two BNCT sessions. Within three months of the first BNCT, the tumor area remained stable, and pre-existing telangiectasia completely disappeared. No irreversible adverse effects of BNCT were observed. Despite ongoing dose exploration, this study highlights BNCT's therapeutic potential for ACC-related liver lesions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Liver transplantation for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with unresectable liver-only disease, with recent trials demonstrating 5-year overall survival rates of 55% to 83%. Surgical resection remains the only curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but its applicability is limited, with only 25% of patients eligible. However, this approach remains investigational with limited global experience and has never been implemented in the Middle East region. Recently, liver transplantation (LT) has emerged as a potential curative option for select patients with unresectable liver-only metastases. This report highlights the potential for liver transplantation to serve as a curative modality in highly selected patients with CRLM and demonstrates its feasibility in a new geographic region. We report the first case in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region of a 41-year-old male with unresectable CRLM who underwent LT following an aggressive multimodal pretransplant protocol. The patient was initially treated at an outside facility for synchronous left-sided colorectal cancer with liver metastases, achieving complete remission after FOLFOX chemotherapy. He subsequently developed 2 liver recurrences: the first in July 2023, with 17 metastases managed at the outside facility by surgical resection and chemotherapy; and the second in October 2023, with 40 metastases, treated with systemic chemotherapy and trans arterial radioembolization (TARE-Y90). He received additional treatment with ablative liver-directed therapies consistent with the "Cleveland Protocol." The patient subsequently underwent orthotopic liver transplantation. His postoperative course was complicated with moderate acute cellular rejection, which was successfully treated, and he was discharged on post-operative day 16. This case demonstrates the successful implementation of liver transplantation for CRLM in the Gulf region, achieving disease-free survival at 4-month follow-up despite high-risk biological features typically associated with poor prognosis. It illustrates the feasibility and potential benefit of LT for unresectable CRLM in carefully selected patients, following an aggressive pretransplant locoregional therapy protocol modeled after the Cleveland Clinic approach. Key success factors included rigorous patient selection using established criteria (Oslo score 0, low Fong score, low PET-MTV), intensive pretransplant optimization with multimodal therapy, and experienced multidisciplinary management of post-transplant complications. With careful patient selection and integration of systemic and liver-directed therapies to achieve maximal disease control, this strategy may help expand transplant eligibility, possibly offering a curative approach. This case provides valuable regional data for the evolving role of transplant oncology in colorectal cancer management in a resource-limited setting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The use of perioperative anesthetic drugs may influence the prognosis of cancer patients, but the expression characteristics and clinical significance of their associated target genes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. This study aims to establish a molecular subtyping system based on perioperative anesthesia-related drug target genes (PARDTGs) and systematically evaluate their potential value in HCC prognosis, immune microenvironment, and drug response. To assess HCC prognosis, we established a PAR-DTG Score derived from PARDTGs. Initial screening in the Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma and GSE14520 cohorts employed differential expression analysis, followed by univariate Cox and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression to identify prognostic genes. Comprehensive characterization of high- and low-risk groups was subsequently performed, integrating immune infiltration analyses, functional enrichment, tumor mutational burden evaluation, and drug sensitivity predictions to elucidate their distinct molecular and clinical features. A prognostic model based on a PARDTG-derived prognostic signature consisting of five genes (CD24, MCM5, PPARGC1A, SLC22A7, and VNN2) was constructed and demonstrated robust predictive performance across two independent cohorts. Patients in the high-risk group exhibited significantly reduced overall survival and enrichment in cell cycle-related pathways (e.g., E2F targets and G2M checkpoint), whereas the low-risk group showed significant enrichment in metabolic pathways (e.g., fatty acid metabolism and bile acid metabolism). Immune microenvironment analysis revealed elevated expression of B cells, CD8 The prognostic model constructed based on PAR-DTG Score effectively distinguishes survival risks among HCC patients and reveals its connections with the immune microenvironment, molecular mechanisms, and drug responses, providing preliminary insights for developing personalized treatment strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abnormal osteopontin (OPN) expression has been implicated in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. In this study, we assessed the prognostic value and biological functions of OPN in HCC. We also identified that A20 interacts with OPN and promotes OPN ubiquitination and protein degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. The reduction in OPN levels induced by A20 attenuates OPN-associated proliferative and migratory phenotypes in HCC cells. Notably, advanced HCC tissues exhibited elevated OPN levels, while A20 expression showed variable patterns in clinical samples. In the clinical cohort, high OPN expression was associated with poorer overall survival, while high A20 expression was also unexpectedly associated with unfavorable prognosis. Combined analysis of OPN and A20 expression provided complementary prognostic stratification for HCC patients. Consequently, our results reveal a mechanism involving OPN ubiquitination and suggest that the OPN/A20 expression profile may provide prognostic stratification for patients after HCC resection. Considering the significance of OPN expression in HCC, our research also provides insights into potential therapeutic strategies for HCC.

Medical oncology (Northwood, London, England) · 2026 Oct 8 · Huang T, Li Q, Yu Z 等
意义与启示：Cancer-associated fibroblasts in therapeutic resistance of hepatocellular carcinoma: evidence, mechanisms, and translational implications
等级评估：C（一般性研究或早期探索） ｜ IF：未获取 ｜ 类型：综述 ｜ 评分：24/100
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to treat because responses to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are limited and heterogeneous. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can influence therapeutic responses through paracrine signaling, immune regulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling, but CAF-driven tumor progression should not be equated with therapeutic resistance. This review critically evaluates HCC-specific evidence according to defined drug exposure, treatment-related outcomes, and functional rescue. The most mechanistically resolved direct resistance mechanisms involve CAF-derived SPP1, which activates integrin-PKCα-dependent bypass signaling during sorafenib or lenvatinib treatment; CAF-derived CXCL12, which reduces sorafenib-induced apoptosis through CXCR4-dependent FOLR1 upregulation; and CAF-derived fibronectin extra domain A, which activates NF-κB-SHMT1-dependent redox adaptation during sorafenib exposure, with TLR4 proposed as the upstream receptor. These pathways are supported by genetic or pharmacological interventions that restore TKI sensitivity. By contrast, POSTN⁺ CAFs are associated with IL-6/IL-6R/STAT3-dependent macrophage recruitment, increased macrophage SPP1 expression, immune exclusion, and reduced ICI responsiveness, although selective reversal of this CAF program remains unproven. Progression-associated and cross-cancer findings are therefore considered separately from established resistance mechanisms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have reshaped systemic therapy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but durable benefit remains limited to a subset of patients because of tumor-intrinsic and microenvironmental mechanisms of immune resistance. Canonical epigenetic and epitranscriptomic alterations, including DNA methylation, histone modifications and chromatin remodeling, and epitranscriptomic RNA modifications, can influence tumor immune visibility by regulating antigen presentation, interferon responses, chemokine production, T-cell recruitment and function, and immunosuppressive programs in myeloid and stromal cells. This review critically evaluates HCC-specific evidence linking these regulatory mechanisms to immune checkpoint responsiveness. Emphasis is placed on crosstalk among DNA methylation, histone/chromatin regulation, and N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-dependent pathways; transcriptional-epigenetic stabilization of T-cell dysfunction; and epigenetic or epitranscriptomic remodeling of myeloid and stromal compartments, including cancer-associated fibroblasts. We further evaluate candidate therapeutic targets using a tiered evidence framework that integrates molecular association, mechanistic validation, pharmacologic validation, evidence from ICI-combination studies, and clinical validation. We assess therapeutic targets by evidence maturity and discuss emerging combination strategies and HCC-specific translational challenges, including chronic liver disease, limited hepatic reserve, and biomarker-guided patient selection. Although preclinical studies support several candidate mechanisms for modulating ICI responsiveness, mature clinical evidence for epigenetic-ICI combinations in HCC remains limited. These strategies should therefore be regarded as mechanistically compelling but clinically unproven and require rigorously designed, biomarker-integrated HCC trials with pharmacodynamic confirmation of immune reprogramming and careful safety evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The treatment strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) remains controversial because of its the dismal prognosis. This study aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) plus molecular-targeted agents (MTA) with or without hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) as a first-line treatment for HCC with PVTT. This nationwide retrospective cohort study utilized a target trial emulation framework with a clone-censor-weighting (CCW) approach and was conducted in 36 centers across China. The study population comprised patients diagnosed with HCC and PVTT who received HAIC in combination with ICIs and MTA (HAIC-ICIs-MTA) or ICIs plus MTA (ICIs-MTA) from June 2018 to December 2024. The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS), which was evaluated through restricted mean survival time (RMST) with bootstrapping. Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety profiles. This study included a total of 1649 HCC patients (614 in the HAIC-ICIs-MTA group and 1035 in the ICIs-MTA group). After CCW, the median OS of the HAIC-ICIs-MTA group was 23.3 months, whereas that of the ICIs-MTA group was 16.4 months. The difference in RMST for OS was 7.4 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.5-11.7, bootstrapped P<0.001). The HAIC-ICIs-MTA group also had a significantly longer median PFS (8.7 months vs. 6.2 months, bootstrapped P=0.002) with an RMST of 2.6 months (95% CI: 0.9-4.5), and a higher ORR (38.9% vs. 22.7%, P<0.001) as per the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors Version 1.1. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 243 patients in the HAIC-ICIs-MTA group (39.6%) and 335 patients in the ICIs-MTA group (32.4%). HAIC in combination with ICIs and MTA is associated with improved survival and an acceptable safety profile compared to ICIs plus MTA alone, supporting this regimen as a promising treatment strategy for HCC patients with PVTT that warrants further prospective validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Up to 40% of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH)-associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) occurs in the absence of cirrhosis. Yet the biological features that underlie non-cirrhotic MASH-to-HCC progression remain poorly understood. We sought to define the cellular and molecular programs associated with non-cirrhotic MASH-to-HCC progression. We integrated histopathological and biochemical assessments, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, serum cytokine profiling, and multiplex immunohistochemistry in Gubra-Amylin-NASH diet-fed mice that remained HCC-naïve or developed non-cirrhotic HCC. Key findings were evaluated in an independent human cohort of non-cirrhotic MASH and MASH-HCC. Body composition metrics, fibrosis severity, histopathology and liver injury markers poorly distinguished HCC-progressors from non-progressors. In contrast, bulk transcriptomics identified prominent immune dysregulation in cancer-primed adjacent non-tumor liver. Single-cell RNA-sequencing revealed coordinated hyperinflammatory reprogramming characterized by loss of Trem2 Non-cirrhotic MASH-to-HCC progression is associated with coordinated hyperinflammatory reprogramming across immune and stromal compartments. Myeloid-derived IL-1β is a central signaling axis within the cancer-permissive MASH microenvironment, providing a potential basis for HCC risk stratification and preventive intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Liver-directed therapy (LDT) is an essential component of multimodal management of colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), yet older adults are less likely to receive liver-directed or curative-intent treatment. We evaluated presentation, treatment patterns, and outcomes among elderly patients with CRLM. We retrospectively reviewed patients with CRLM treated at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center and Parkland Memorial Hospital from 2016 to 2023. Liver-directed therapy was defined as liver resection, hepatic artery infusion pump therapy, ablation, liver-directed radiation including external beam radiation and stereotactic body radiation, transarterial chemoembolization, and/or Y-90 radioembolization. The primary outcome was overall survival (OS); the secondary outcome was receipt of LDT. Cox proportional hazards regression identified factors associated with OS among patients aged ≥70 years. Among 852 patients, 710 were aged <70 years and 142 were aged ≥70 years. Liver metastasis number, bilobar involvement, CEA level, and extrahepatic disease were similar between age groups. Older adults were less likely to receive LDT than younger patients (20% vs. 40%, p < 0.001). Among patients who underwent hepatic resection, perioperative outcomes were similar by age. Among older adults, LDT was associated with longer median OS than no LDT (44 vs. 9 months, p < 0.001). Among patients receiving LDT, median OS was comparable between age groups (44 vs. 52 months, p = 0.19). Performance status, CEA ≥200 ng/mL, chemotherapy, and LDT were independently associated with OS. Older adults with CRLM were less likely to receive LDT. Among selected older adults, receipt of LDT was associated with longer OS than no LDT. Chronological age alone should not preclude consideration of LDT.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
As the role of transarterial radioembolization (TARE) in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) beyond Milan criteria remains undefined, this study compared preoperative TARE and chemoembolization (TACE) with primary resection to establish the optimal management strategy. We retrospectively analyzed HCC patients who did not meet the Milan criteria and underwent primary liver resection, preoperative TACE, or preoperative TARE. Overall survival (OS), time to recurrence (TTR), and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression with inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). A total of 226 patients were included (primary resection, n = 127; preoperative TACE, n = 52; preoperative TARE, n = 47), with a median follow-up of 37.2 months. After IPTW, baseline characteristics were well balanced. Median OS was not reached in the primary resection and preoperative TARE, but was 60.7 months in the preoperative TACE group. Compared with primary resection, preoperative TACE was associated with worse OS (adjusted HR [aHR]: 2.72; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.39-5.33; p = 0.004), whereas OS with preoperative TARE was comparable (aHR: 1.14; 95% CI: 0.50-2.55; p = 0.76) after IPTW. Similarly, TTR and RFS were significantly worse in the preoperative TACE (both p = 0.02), whereas no significant differences were observed between the preoperative TARE and primary liver resection groups after IPTW (p = 0.59 and p = 0.57). Preoperative TARE showed no significant difference in survival from primary liver resection in resectable HCC beyond the Milan criteria and may serve as a reasonable alternative strategy when upfront surgery is not feasible. Question Optimal treatment for resectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) beyond the Milan criteria is controversial. The role of preoperative transarterial radioembolization (TARE) compared with chemoembolization (TACE) or upfront resection remains unclear. Findings Preoperative TARE achieved survival outcomes comparable to primary resection, whereas preoperative TACE was associated with significantly inferior overall and recurrence-free survival. Clinical relevance Preoperative TARE demonstrates survival outcomes comparable to primary resection. It serves as a reasonable therapeutic alternative for resectable hepatocellular carcinoma beyond the Milan criteria, offering effective local control when immediate surgery is not feasible.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Intratumoral granulomas (ITGs) are rarely described in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and may obscure malignancy in limited biopsy specimens. We retrospectively reviewed 614 HCCs diagnosed from 2010 to 2023 to identify tumors with ITG and compared clinicopathologic features and overall survival with HCCs lacking ITG. ITG was identified in 32/614 cases (5.2%). All granulomas were non-necrotizing; 3/32 cases also had granulomas in background liver. No patient had sarcoidosis, primary biliary cholangitis, or documented infection. Patients with ITG were predominantly male (23/32, 71.9%), with a mean age of 67.5 years. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) was the most common underlying liver disease (13/32, 40.6%). Compared with HCCs without ITG, HCCs with ITG were significantly associated with MASLD (13/32, 40.6% vs 98/582, 16.8%; P = 0.0072), steatohepatitic subtype (22/32, 68.8% vs 119/576, 20.7%; P < 0.0001), intratumoral lymphocytic inflammation (26/28, 92.9% vs 366/572, 64.0%; P = 0.0001), and at least moderate peritumoral inflammation (11/18, 61.1% vs 60/255, 23.5%; P = 0.003). Granuloma-associated inflammation was T-cell predominant and enriched for CD4-positive T cells. In univariable analysis, patients with ITG had improved overall survival (P = 0.004); however, the association was attenuated and did not reach statistical significance after adjustment for age, tumor size, stage, and MASLD etiology (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.20-1.11; P = 0.098). Among stage II tumors, patients with ITG had borderline improved survival (P = 0.05). Prominent ITG may mask HCC in biopsy specimens. These findings support ITG as an uncommon but recognizable HCC-associated tumor microenvironment enriched in MASLD-related steatohepatitic HCC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) coinfection exacerbates clinical outcomes in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients. With emerging HDV-targeted therapeutics, accurate prevalence and clinical impact data are essential. In this study, the seroprevalence, clinical significance, and molecular characteristics of HDV were assessed in South Korean patients across the spectrum of liver disease. This two-center retrospective study included 526 patients with CHB: non-cirrhotic CHB (n=100), cirrhotic CHB (liver cirrhosis, n=100), and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC; n=326). Serum samples (2012 to 2024) were analyzed for anti-HDV antibodies and HDV RNA using commercial assays and quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, followed by full-length genomic sequencing. The median patient age was 58.0 years, and 71.3% of the patients were male. The overall anti-HDV seroprevalence was 2.7% (14/526). Prevalence did not differ significantly across disease groups: 2.0% in non-cirrhotic CHB, 4.0% in cirrhotic CHB, and 2.5% in HCC (p=0.733). Notably, in HCC patients, anti-HDV seroprevalence was significantly higher in advanced stages (Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer [BCLC] C-D) than in very early-to-intermediate stages (BCLC 0-B) (5.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.024). HDV RNA was detected in only one patient (0.2% of the total cohort; 7.1% of anti-HDV-positive patients). Phylogenetic analysis characterized the first full-length HDV genotype 1 genome in South Korea, which clustered with East Asian strains. Anti-HDV seroprevalence in Korean CHB patients is 2.7%, whereas viremic prevalence is 0.2%. Anti-HDV positivity is linked to male sex and advanced HCC stage. These findings emphasize the need for HDV screening in patients with advanced liver disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) refractory to locoregional therapies remains a major clinical challenge. This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of locoregional high-dose autologous natural killer (NK) cell therapy combined with hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (HAIC) in patients with locally advanced HCC. This open-label, multicenter, phase IIa study enrolled patients with locally advanced HCC refractory to standard care. Patients achieving stable disease (SD) or better after two HAIC cycles (5-fluorouracil and cisplatin) underwent two additional HAIC cycles followed by hepatic arterial NK cell infusion for up to two cycles. The primary endpoint was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed objective response rate (ORR). Secondary endpoints included investigator-assessed ORR, disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), time to progression (TTP), overall survival (OS), safety, and immunologic response. Tumor response was assessed per modified RECIST for HCC. Of 17 enrolled patients, 16 were evaluable. IRC-assessed ORR was 68.75% (exact 95% confidence interval, 41.34-88.98) [complete response (CR): 18.75%; partial response (PR): 50.00%], and investigator-assessed ORR was 62.50%. Both assessments yielded a DCR of 100%. Median DOR was 12.65 and 10.48 months by IRC and investigator assessment, respectively. Median investigator-assessed TTP was 16.82 months; IRC-assessed TTP was not reached. Median OS was 24.05 months. No severe NK cell-related toxicities were observed. Locoregional high-dose autologous NK cell therapy following HAIC showed promising antitumor activity and an acceptable profile in selected patients with locally advanced HCC. These findings warrant validation in randomized trials designed to isolate the incremental contribution of NK cell therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has demonstrated efficacy in clinical cancer therapy; however, a significant proportion of cancer patients do not respond to ICB. One contributing factor to this lack of response is the impairment of IFN-γ signaling within cancer cells. A20 acts as a negative regulator of IFN-γ signaling. Our study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which A20 exerts its negative regulatory effect on IFN-γ signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cells. Bioinformatic analysis revealed that A20 expression in HCC cell lines is inversely associated with the activation of IFN-γ signaling. Functional loss and gain experiments demonstrated that A20 inhibits IFN-γ signaling in HCC cells. The interaction between A20 and STAT1 was assessed using Co-Immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays and bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BioFC) assays. Our results also indicated that A20 suppresses the expression of downstream molecules involved in IFN-γ signaling, such as CXCL9, CXCL10, and HLA-ABC, in HCC cells. Additionally, enforced expression of A20 in HCC cells inhibited anti-tumor immunity in a mouse model of HCC. Bioinformatic analysis suggests that A20 may negatively regulate IFN-γ signaling in HCC cells from human HCC cohorts. Collectively, our study uncovers a novel mechanism whereby A20 inhibits IFN-γ signaling in HCC cells through direct binding with STAT1. These findings enhance our understanding of the regulatory mechanisms of IFN-γ signaling in cancer cells and provide insights for designing strategies to enhance the effectiveness of ICB therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Parenchyma-sparing hepatectomy planning depends on accurate resection zones that preserve functional liver tissue without compromising oncological margins. This work investigates how different levels of anatomical and functional information complexity influence resection zone prediction for parenchyma-sparing surgical planning for primary liver cancer. We compare three modeling paradigms: a geometric distance-based approach, an explicit perfusion-based method using vascular anatomy, and a deep learning-based model built on the U-Net architecture. All methods operate on segmentation-derived representations of the liver, tumor, and vessels. Performance is evaluated using overlap- and distance-based metrics. The distance-based model produces predictions with limited surface deviation (HD None of the models is universally outperforming the other two for parenchyma-sparing resection planning. Deep learning shows strong predictive performance, particularly for larger resection volumes, while geometric and perfusion-based models offer greater interpretability and clinical controllability. The distance-based approach is well suited for maximal parenchyma-sparing resections, whereas perfusion-based modeling is advantageous for tumors near vessels with potential perfusion loss. Our results highlight variations due to different surgical strategies and can thus provide valuable guidance for individual patient's surgery planning.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Clinical trials in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) often exclude patients with poor prognostic factors, including impaired liver function, poor functional status or main trunk portal vein thrombosis (Vp4). The dual immune checkpoint inhibitor regimen STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) is a standard-of-care treatment for first-line uHCC. The phase IIIb SIERRA (NCT05883644) study previously reported early safety of STRIDE in participants of poor prognosis. Here, we present safety and efficacy results from the primary analysis of the SIERRA study. Adults with uHCC with either Child-Pugh B7/B8 liver function (Child-Pugh B7/B8 cohort), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 2 (ECOG PS 2 cohort) or Vp4 (Vp4 cohort) were enrolled. All participants received STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg plus durvalumab 1500 mg once, followed by durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary endpoints were Grade 3 or 4 adverse events possibly related to study treatment within 6 months of treatment initiation (Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months) and objective response rate (ORR; data cut-off: 22 September 2025). In total, 111 participants were included (Child-Pugh B7/B8 n = 44, ECOG PS 2 n = 47, Vp4 n = 20). The incidence of Grade 3/4 PRAEs ≤6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]) was 19.8% (12.9-28.5): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 18.2% (8.2-32.7); ECOG PS 2, 19.1% (9.1-33.3); and Vp4, 25.0% (8.7-49.1). ORR (95% CI) was 14.4% (8.5-22.4): Child-Pugh B7/B8, 6.8% (1.4-18.7); ECOG PS 2, 21.3% (10.7-35.7); and Vp4, 15.0% (3.2-37.9). SIERRA safety and efficacy findings were indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need. Participants with poor prognosis (e.g. Child-Pugh B/C, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status >1 or main trunk portal vein thrombosis [Vp4]) remain underrepresented in global, phase III trials despite comprising up to 65% of patients with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (uHCC) in clinical practice. To address this unmet need, the phase IIIb SIERRA study (NCT05883644) evaluated STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab) in participants with poor prognostic factors. Safety and efficacy findings as per the co-primary endpoints are indicative of a favourable risk-benefit profile for STRIDE in this participant population with a high unmet need, with an incidence of Grade 3 or 4 PRAEs within 6 months of 19.8% and ORR of 14.4% in the total population. This is the first prospective interventional study to provide data informing the safety and efficacy of STRIDE in patients with uHCC in a previously underrepresented population of poor prognosis that are excluded from other phase III trials. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is associated with higher incidence of colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM); prohibitin 1 (PHB1) defends against CRLM yet its role in ALD and ALD-CRLM is poorly understood and was investigated here. In human, murine, and in vitro ALD models, cytosolic and nuclear PHB1 were depleted, whereas mitochondrial PHB1 was preserved despite a loss in mitochondrial mass. Nuclear PHB1 loss was driven by CRM1-mediated export, and blocking this interaction with a PHB1 nuclear export signal (NES) peptide retained nuclear PHB1, ameliorating both ALD and ALD-CRLM. PHB1 NES prevented depletion of nuclear methionine adenosyltransferase α1, oxidative stress, and induction of matrix metalloproteinase 7 (MMP-7) and multiple oncogenes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing of NIAAA diet-fed mouse livers and spatial transcriptomics of ALD-CRLM mice livers revealed that PHB1 NES treatment mitigated alcohol-induced metabolic and oncogenic stress, attenuated pro-inflammation and pro-fibrogenic responses, remodeled immunosuppressive microenvironment and contributed to overall hepatoprotection. These findings identify nuclear PHB1 depletion as a driver and a promising therapeutic target in ALD and ALD-CRLM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic reprogramming and lipid remodeling are increasingly recognized as key processes underlying carcinogenesis and cancer treatment failure. The liver, as a central hub for lipid metabolism and homeostasis, is particularly susceptible to such alterations. Accordingly, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits extensive metabolic dysregulation and lipid remodeling, contributing to resistance to systemic therapies, including sorafenib. This study characterized histopathological and metabolic signatures across HCC carcinogenesis stages using a diethylnitrosamine/thioacetamide-induced rat model. Histopathological analysis confirmed gradual progression from inflammation to cirrhosis and finally HCC, based on non-alcoholic fatty liver disease activity scoring and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis fibrosis staging. Metabolomic profiling revealed stage-specific metabolic patterns throughout disease progression, with a marked shift toward lipid-centric metabolism during fibrosis and in sorafenib-persistent tumors, defined here as cancer cells that survive sorafenib treatment. These metabolic changes highlight the role of lipid remodeling in both early carcinogenesis and systemic treatment tolerance. Furthermore, lipidomic analysis of sorafenib-persistent HCC demonstrated significant accumulation of lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC)(20:4) and depletion of precursor phosphatidylcholine species, demonstrating alterations to the phosphatidylcholine-lysophosphatidylcholine axis. Given that cytosolic phospholipase A2 (cPLA2) is a key enzyme that hydrolyzes phosphatidylcholine to generate lysophosphatidylcholine, we hypothesized that cPLA2 may contribute to the observed lipid imbalance. Mechanistic validation in sorafenib-treated HepG2 cells using the cPLA2 inhibitor AACOCF3 showed increased sorafenib sensitivity, enhanced apoptosis, and reduced clonogenicity upon cPLA2 inhibition. Collectively, these findings identify phosphatidylcholine-lysophosphatidylcholine axis alteration as a potential driver of cancer cell survival under sorafenib treatment and highlight lipid metabolic reprogramming as a sorafenib-re-sensitization target in HCC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is highly prevalent, and fibrosis stage is the strongest determinant of liver-related outcomes, hepatocellular carcinoma and mortality. Liver biopsy remains the reference standard for staging, but it is invasive, subject to sampling and observer variability. These limitations have accelerated the use of noninvasive tests (NITs) across various settings. This review summarizes the past, present and future of the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index in SLD. We reviewed the development of serum-based fibrosis assessment, validation of FIB-4 across SLD subtypes, its incorporation into clinical pathways, real-world performance and potential role in precision therapy and longitudinal risk assessment. Initially derived in patients with HIV/hepatitis C coinfection using age, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and platelet count, FIB-4 has since been validated across SLD populations. FIB-4 generally provides moderate discrimination for advanced fibrosis and high negative predictive value (NPV) when used with dual thresholds and age-adjusted cutoffs. Modern care pathways operationalize FIB-4 as the first-line triage test, followed by transient elastography or another second line test for indeterminate or elevated results, with specialty referral and selective biopsy reserved for diagnostic uncertainty or discordant testing. In the precision therapy era, FIB-4 remains a scalable front-door test but should not serve as a stand-alone selector for drug eligibility; confirmatory staging is required to identify F2-F3 disease and exclude cirrhosis. Future directions include trajectory-based monitoring, integration with elastography and multi-analyte biomarkers, and selective layering of genetic risk to refine prognosis in intermediate and high-risk strata.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Physical activity is associated with lower risk of liver cancer, but obtaining an unbiased estimate of the causal effect is challenging due to the competing risk of death due to any other cause. We performed a causal competing risk analysis to estimate the total effect of physical activity on risk of liver cancer in the presence of competing deaths. Data were included for 263,184 participants (870 liver cancers) in the NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study. Total effects in the presence of competing deaths were estimated on the risk difference (RD) scale as the differences, by age, in standardised cause-specific cumulative incidence functions of liver cancer had all participants engaged in ≥ 4 h/week of moderate- to vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) versus < 4 h/week. There were an estimated 18 per 100,000 fewer liver cancer cases for ≥ 4 h/week of MVPA versus < 4 h/week (95% confidence interval [CI]: 6.2, 29.9) by age 67 years (average age of diagnosis in the United States), and an estimated 58 per 100,000 fewer cases (95% CI: 21.1, 95.8) by age 78 years (average US life expectancy). Estimated RDs were larger in older than younger age groups (e.g., RD per 100,000 at age 85 years = -79.0, 95% CI: -133.4, -24.7; at age 55 years = -2.0, 95% CI: -4.5, 0.6). Our findings strengthen the evidence for physical activity reducing risk of liver cancer. Increasing physical activity at the population level may reduce the growing, global burden of liver cancer.
